title: 10-minute office workout
intro: Sitting long hours at the office makes your body stiff and you move less. This 10-minute routine can be done next to your desk, without changing clothes and without sweating much.
muscles: Light full-body work: legs, glutes, chest, arms, shoulders and back. It also helps boost blood flow.
steps: Minutes 1-2: Walk on the spot or to the pantry and back, swinging your arms.
Minutes 3-4: Squat to a chair, 10 times, rest a bit, repeat.
Minutes 5-6: Desk push-ups (make sure the desk is sturdy), 10 times, repeat.
Minutes 7-8: Calf raises 15 times, then roll your shoulders backwards 10 times.
Minutes 9-10: Chest stretch in a door frame and a slow seated twist on your chair, 30 seconds each side.
mistakes: Using a chair with wheels for squats or a wobbly desk for push-ups.
Going too fast until you're out of breath and sweaty before a meeting.
Holding your breath. Breathe normally throughout each move.
easier: Do every move halfway only, or pick 2-3 moves for 5 minutes.
harder: Repeat the routine twice a day, or increase squats and push-ups up to 15 reps.
dose: 10 minutes, 1 to 2 times a day on workdays. On top of that, get up and move for 2-3 minutes every hour.
safety: Stop if you feel dizzy, have chest pain or unusual shortness of breath. If you have heart, blood pressure or joint problems, check with your doctor first.

faq.q: I'm shy to do this in front of colleagues. What to do?
faq.a: Do it in the pantry, the stairwell or an empty room. Calf raises and shoulder rolls can even be done while standing at the printer without anyone noticing.

faq.q: Is 10 minutes enough to lose weight?
faq.a: It helps add to your daily movement, and every bit of movement counts. But weight loss depends more on your food portions and overall activity across the week.

faq.q: When is the best time to do it?
faq.a: After lunch or when you feel sleepy in the afternoon works well. Choose a time that's easy for you to repeat every day.
